test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to Mahatma Jyotiba Phule on his birth anniversary. Phule is best known for his contributions to which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Social Reform and Anti-Caste Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Jyotiba Phule was an Indian social reformer, thinker, and writer who significantly contributed to the **abolition of the caste system** and the upliftment of marginalized communities.
 
• He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, pioneered the cause of **women's education in India**, establishing the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
• Phule is best known for his efforts to eradicate untouchability and caste-based discrimination through his writings and activism.
 
• He founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873 to promote social equality and fight against caste oppression.
 
• Jyotiba Phule's literary works, such as "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), criticized the social hierarchies and supported the empowerment of oppressed communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-Caste Movement:** It refers to the various social and political movements that aimed to eradicate caste-based discrimination and untouchability in India, led by reformers like Jyotiba Phule, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and Periyar.
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj:** Founded by Phule in 1873, this organization worked for the rights of women, Dalits, and other marginalized communities, emphasizing the need for education and social reform.
 
• **Savitribai Phule:** Jyotiba’s wife and collaborator, she was one of India's first female educators and a key figure in the movement for women's rights and education.
 
• **Gulamgiri (Slavery):** A book written by Phule in 1873, it draws parallels between the oppression of African slaves and India’s lower castes, calling for social justice and equality.
 
• **Legacy:** Jyotiba Phule's contributions to social reform laid the foundation for later movements against caste discrimination, inspiring leaders like Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in the Indian freedom struggle and social justice movement.
